topics.title: Resolved: EAPPasswordError with IKEv2, EAP-TTLS and FortiAuthenticator 2FA
topics.summary: I recently encountered and resolved the following issue, and I am sharing the troubleshooting process because the FortiClient error did not immediately indicate the actual cause.EnvironmentFortiClient EMS: 7.4.8 FortiClient for Windows: 7.4.8 FortiAuthenticator: 6.6.9 FortiGate VM: FortiOS 7.4.13 VPN type: IKEv2 IPsec Authentication method: EAP-TTLS User source: LDAP/Active Directory Two-factor authentication: FortiToken managed through FortiAuthenticatorIssueWhen I tried to establish the VPN connection using a domain account, FortiClient returned the following error:EAPPasswordErrorThe authentication process failed, and the VPN connection could not be established.Since I was taking over an existing installation, I was not yet fully familiar with every step of the authentication flow between FortiClient, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, and the LDAP server.Troubleshooting performedI initially verified the following points: The FortiGate was reachable from the client’s public IP address. A direct LDAP authentication test from the FortiGate was successful for both connectivity and credential validation. EAP-TTLS was selected in the VPN profile distributed through FortiClient EMS. EAP-TTLS was enabled in the FortiAuthenticator RADIUS policy, while EAP-MSCHAPv2 was disabled. The default realm configured in the RADIUS policy was associated with the correct LDAP identity source. During an authentication test from FortiAuthenticator, I received an error indicating that the user could not be found in the imported users database. I also found an Access-Reject event containing the message “User Locked”, but I could not confirm whether it was related to the same VPN authentication attempt. Since the direct LDAP test was successful, I initially suspected that the authentication request was not being processed correctly at some point in the chain between IKEv2, EAP-TTLS, RADIUS, FortiAuthenticator, and LDAP.SolutionI eventually found that the problem was related to the way the second authentication factor had to be entered.When EAP-TTLS/PAP is used with two-factor authentication through FortiAuthenticator, FortiClient does not display a separate prompt for the FortiToken code.The LDAP password and the current OTP must be entered consecutively in the same password field:LDAP password + OTPFor example:MyPassword123456After entering the LDAP password followed immediately by the current OTP, the authentication completed successfully and the IKEv2 IPsec VPN connection was established.The behavior and solution are documented in the following Fortinet Technical Tips:Technical Tip: Multi-Factor Authentication support for Windows FortiClient with LDAP (EAP-TTLS)https://community.fortinet.com/fortigate-3/technical-tip-multi-factor-authentication-support-for-windows-forticlient-with-ldap-eap-ttls-212498Technical Tip: How to resolve the “EAP authentication failed due to missing token” error when using EAP-TTLS/PAP + 2FA Authenticationhttps://community.fortinet.com/fortiauthenticator-8/technical-tip-how-to-resolve-the-eap-authentication-failed-due-to-missing-token-error-when-using-eap-ttls-pap-2fa-authentication-216311?tid=216311&fid=8In my case, the issue was not related to LDAP connectivity or realm selection. It was caused by the way the second authentication factor had to be provided when using EAP-TTLS with FortiAuthenticator.The EAPPasswordError message did not immediately indicate the actual cause, and the successful direct LDAP test initially led me to investigate other parts of the authentication flow.Has anyone else encountered the same behavior or received a different FortiClient error in a similar configuration?I hope this information can help anyone troubleshooting the same issue.

topics.title: Rx Discards increase on access FortiSwitch uplink ports when fortilink-neighbor-detect is set to FortiLink
topics.summary: DescriptionThe Rx Discards counter increases on the uplink ports of an access FortiSwitch when the FortiGate FortiLink interface uses fortilink-neighbor-detect fortilink. Also, how to stop the increase by changing the setting to LLDP.ScopeFortiGate and FortiSwitch units managed over FortiLink, with fortilink-neighbor-detect set to FortiLink.SolutionSymptoms:The Rx Discards counter increases steadily on the uplink ports of the access FortiSwitch. These are the ports that connect to the distribution or core FortiSwitch.The Rx Discards counter does not increase on the access (downlink) ports.The uplink ports show no CRC, input, or output errors.The Rx Discards counter stops increasing after setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to LLDP on the FortiGate.Cause:When setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to FortiLink, the FortiGate and FortiSwitch units exchange proprietary FortiLink protocol frames over the FortiLink and ISL trunks. The access FortiSwitch receives these frames on its uplink ports, handles them itself instead of forwarding them, and adds them to the Rx Discards counter.When setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to LLDP, the FortiGate and FortiSwitch units use standard LLDP frames for neighbor detection. The FortiSwitch does not add these frames to the Rx Discards counter.Verification:On the FortiGate, check which neighbor detection method the FortiLink interface uses:show full system interface | grep neighborOn the access FortiSwitch, find the uplink trunk and its member ports:diagnose switch trunk summary show switch trunkOn the access FortiSwitch, reset the counters on each uplink port, wait a few minutes, and check the counters again:diagnose switch physical-ports set-counter-zero diagnose switch physical-ports port-stats list Rx Discards: diagnose switch physical-ports list drops Rx Discards: drops set lldp-reception enable set lldp-transmission enable set fortilink-neighbor-detect lldp next endOn the access FortiSwitch, reset the counters on each uplink port and confirm that the Rx Discards counter either stops increasing or no longer increases at the same rate as before the change:diagnose switch physical-ports set-counter-zero diagnose switch physical-ports port-stats list diagnose switch physical-ports list Notes:The increase in the Rx Discards counter does not disrupt production traffic.Changing fortilink-neighbor-detect can briefly interrupt traffic, so plan the change for a maintenance window.Enable LLDP before you change the detection method. If changing the method without enabling LLDP, the managed FortiSwitch units go offline.A FortiLink interface based on a hardware switch does not offer the fortilink-neighbor-detect option.Related Article:Troubleshooting Tip: How to interpret RX drops on FortiSwitch devices

topics.title: Metadata variables in CLI scripts use global or default values instead of mapped (per-device/VDOM) values
topics.summary: Description How metadata variables works in a CLI script. Scope FortiManager. Solution Metadata variables referenced inside CLI scripts in FortiManager do not resolve to a device‑specific mapped value when the script is executed on the Device Database. The script applies the value defined for the global context, or the default value if no global value is set — not the value mapped for a specific device or VDOM. Scenario A metadata variable is created with a default value and a per‑device mapped value (e.g. mapped for a root or named VDOM). If used inside a firewall object (e.g. an Address), the variable correctly resolves to the device's mapped value. The same variable used inside a CLI script run on the Device Database resolves to the global value — or the default value when no global value exists — instead of the per‑device/VDOM mapped value. This is an expected behavior. Metadata variables used in CLI scripts executed on the Device Database only support the global context or the default value. VDOM‑context (per‑device/VDOM) mapped values are not resolved within CLI scripts. Below a practical example. This is the metadata variable: FMG_Test # execute fmpolicy print-adom-object 179 3200 test_metadataDump object ttest_metadata] of category dfmg variable] in adom vTEST]:---------------config fmg variableedit "test_metadata"set value "1"config dynamic_mappingedit "Test_Firewall"-"global"set value "5"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"SDWAN"set value "12"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"root"set value "9"nextendnextend Script: config vdomedit SDWANconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendend This script is run on the Device DB on Test_Firewall. Note that the "global" value was used. The values assigned to "root" or "SDWAN" were not used. View the log of script Test: running on device Test_Firewall (Test)-------Executing time: Thu Oct 22 15:33:07 2026-----------Starting log (Run on database)config vdomedit SDWANconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4 nextendendRunning script(Test) on DB success

topics.title: Prevent unnecessary FortiLink frames on FortiSwitch edge ports
topics.summary: DescriptionThe reasons why Managed FortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile may forward unnecessary FortiLink protocol frames (EtherType 0x88FF) to connected end devices. Devices that do not support or process these frames may discard them, resulting in rapidly increasing packet discard counters and unnecessary network traffic.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionFortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile by default.This profile supports automatic Inter-Switch Link (ISL) formation, allowing FortiSwitches to discover each other and establish inter-switch trunks.When this profile is applied to ports connected to end devices that do not require automatic ISL formation, FortiLink protocol frames with EtherType 0x88FF may reach those devices.The receiving devices may discard these frames because the EtherType is unsupported, causing unnecessary increases in packet discard counters.SolutionChange the LLDP profile on affected edge ports from default-auto-isl to default.Important: Do not apply this change indiscriminately to ports connected to other FortiSwitches that rely on automatic ISL formation.Configuration via FortiGate CLIIdentify the FortiSwitch and its connected edge ports.Verify that the ports do not require automatic ISL formation.Apply the following configuration:config switch-controller managed-switch edit config ports edit set lldp-profile "default" next end next endExpected resultUnnecessary FortiLink protocol frames are prevented from reaching connected devices on the affected ports, reducing avoidable frame discards and preventing servers from receiving a flood of unnecessary Ethernet frames.

topics.title: FortiAppSec Cookie Security causing HTTP 403 Forbidden errors
topics.summary: DescriptionEnabling the Set HttpOnly Cookie feature in FortiWeb Cloud may cause applications to return HTTP 403 Forbidden errors if the application relies on JavaScript to read CSRF tokens from cookies.ScopeFortiAppSec Cloud.SolutionSymptomsUsers encounter HTTP 403 Forbidden (Authentication Error) responses on various application pages after a successful login. These errors occur specifically when Cookie Security features are enabled in FortiWeb Cloud. No corresponding security violations or blocks appear in the Web Application Firewall (WAF) event logs, even when the policy is set to Alert mode.Root CauseThe issue is caused by the Set HttpOnly Cookie setting. When this feature is enabled, FortiWeb Cloud adds the HttpOnly flag to cookies passed to the browser. This flag prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie.If the application is designed to read a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token from a cookie using JavaScript, the browser cannot access the token. Consequently, the application receives a request with a missing or empty CSRF token and returns an HTTP 403 Access Denied response. Because this is an application-level authentication failure and not a WAF security block, no events are logged in the FortiWeb Cloud WAF logs.ResolutionDisable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option while maintaining other security settings.Log in to the FortiWeb Cloud console.Navigate to the Cookie Security settings for the affected policy.Disable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option.Keep the Set Secure Cookie option enabled if the application supports it.Save the configuration and test the application functionality.

topics.title: How to create a CLI script that runs automatically after every policy package or device settings installation on FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to create a CLI script on FortiManager and configure it to run automatically on the FortiGate after every device install (policy package or device settings installation).ScopeFortiManager 7.x and 8.x.SolutionSome settings are changed or reverted by an install from FortiManager, or cannot be managed from the policy package or device database. A CLI script that runs directly on the FortiGate after each install can restore the required configuration without a manual step.For this, create a script with the target "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)", then enable "Automatic execute after each device install" in the script schedule.Step 1: Create the scriptGo to "Device Manager" -> Script.Select "Create New".Enter a name for the script (for example, "post-install-script").Set "Type" to "CLI Script".Set "Run script on" to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)".In "Script Detail", enter the CLI commands to run on the FortiGate. For example, for a FortiGate with VDOMs enabled:config vdom edit root config set end next endFor a FortiGate without VDOMs, enter the commands without the "config vdom" and "edit root" lines:config set endSelect "OK".Step 2: Run the script automatically after every installEnable the scheduled and automatic script options in the FortiManager CLI:config system admin setting set show_automatic_script enable set show_schedule_script enable endGo to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts".Right-click the CLI script and select "Schedule Script".Select the FortiGate devices that the script will run on.Select "Enable Automatic execute after each device install".Select "OK".Once enabled, the script runs on the selected FortiGate devices after each install, including every policy package installation and device settings installation. No manual step is needed.VerificationInstall a policy package or the device settings to one of the selected FortiGate devices.When the install finishes, go to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts" and open the script execution history ("Script Log") to check that the script ran on the device.On the FortiGate CLI, check that the configuration was applied. For example:show full | grep Note:"Automatic execute after each device install" is only available when "Run script on" is set to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)". It cannot be used with scripts that target "Policy Package" or "ADOM Database".When "Automatic execute after each device install" is enabled, a time-based schedule (one time, daily, weekly, monthly) cannot be configured for the same script.A script that runs directly on the FortiGate triggers an automatic retrieve back to FortiManager. The policy package status may temporarily show "Unknown".The script runs after the install, so the change is applied on the FortiGate but does not become part of the policy package or the device database in FortiManager. The next install can overwrite it, which is why the script runs after every install.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Certificate-based dialup IPsec authentication fails after upgrading to FortiOS versions 7.6.7 and 7.4.12 when the PKI peer uses cn-type FQDN
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes why, in some scenarios, certificate-based dialup IPsec authentication may fail after upgrading to FortiOS versions 7.6.7 or 7.4.12 when the PKI peer is configured with cn-type FQDN.ScopeFortiGate, certificate-based dialup IPsec VPN.SolutionCertificate-based IPsec VPN utilizes mutual certificate-based authentication to validate the certificate chain presented during the IKE authentication. The accepted CA certificate and Common Name information of client certificate should be configured under the 'config user peer' to be referenced by the IPsec configuration.When a PKI peer uses cn-type FQDN on the Diapup IPsec VPN hub FortiGate, it not only checks the certificate name but also compares the hostname’s mapped IP address with the connecting client’s IP address.For example:config user peer edit "BRANCH-PEER" set ca "VPN-CA" set subject "CN=branch01.example.com" set cn "branch01.example.com" set cn-type FQDN next endFor authentication to succeed, the hub must resolve the peer's Common Name (CN) 'branch01.example.com' to the connecting peer’s IP address as seen by the hub. If the peer is behind NAT, this is the translated source address.In some FortiOS versions earlier than versions 7.4.12 and 7.6.7, the hub could still accept the certificate without enforcing this IP comparison and only verify the Common Name string, which made the certificate verification successful even if the DNS resolution failed or resolve-IP was not matched.After upgrading to FortiOS versions 7.4.12 and 7.6.7, a certificate-name match alone is insufficient when cn-type FQDN is configured.To identify this issue, both IKE and FNBAMD debugging need to be enabled on the hub:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application ike -1 diagnose debug application fnbamd -1 diagnose debug enableThe following output indicates that the certificate name matches, but the client-IP check fails:__check_add_peer-check 'BRANCH-PEER' __RDN_match-Checking 'CN' val 'branch01.example.com' -- match. peer_cn_check-Checking client IP '198.51.100.20' -- no match. __check_add_peer-'BRANCH-PEER' check ret:badIKE subsequently reports:fnbam cert group matching failed certificate validation failed authentication failedIn this example, the 'fnbamd' daemon needs to verify whether the hub resolves 'branch01.example.com' to 198.51.100.20. An unresolved hostname or a mapping to a different address would cause the FQDN/IP validation to fail.Solution:Option 1: Retain FQDN-to-client-IP validation.This is to keep cn-type FQDN and ensure the hub can resolve the certificate hostname to the connecting peer’s IP address. If the DNS resolution is not successful or incorrect, it requires checking the hub’s DNS server configuration, DNS reachability, and the hostname’s DNS records.Option 2: Authenticate by certificate name without IP binding.If the requirement is to validate the trusted certificate and its configured CN independently of the peer’s WAN/NAT address, it is suggested to change the CN type to 'string'. With this setting, the Hub FortiGate will verify the CA certificate chain and the certificate's Common Name (CN) only:config user peer edit "BRANCH-PEER" set ca "VPN-CA" set subject "CN=branch01.example.com" set cn "branch01.example.com" set cn-type string next endRelated documents:Technical Tip: FortiGate Certificate-based IPsec VPN ConfigurationConfiguring a PKI user

topics.title: FortiGate 3G4G models show out of sync warning in HA due to different WWAN IPv6 addresses
topics.summary: Description When LTE-capable FortiGate devices such as the FortiGate 40F-3G4G are in an HA cluster, and each WWAN interface receives a different IPv6 address from the upstream provider, the HA cluster may show as out of sync. This occurs because LTE IPv6 addresses are specific to each member. Scope FortiGate and FortiWiFi models with built-in 3G/4G cellular modems. Solution An HA configuration out-of-sync status does not affect cluster operation or new configuration synchronization. While the error can be cleared temporarily after configuration changes, the issue is expected to recur. In this specific scenario, it is recommended not to run diagnose ha checksum recalculate on affected devices, as this may temporarily overwrite the WWAN IPv6 address of the other cluster unit.The issue occurs because the FortiGate cluster incorrectly considers the IPv6 address to be statically configured and eligible for HA configuration synchronization, even though they are determined dynamically and learned from the internal modem.At the time of writing (October 2026), this issue is scheduled for resolution in FortiOS version 8.0.3 and above. Note that fix schedules are subject to change without notice.

topics.title: Windows updates fails with enabled Forticlient
topics.summary: Since last week we experiencing a lot of problems with Windows updates (mostly Windows 11, but there was one Windows 10 among them as well), specifically KB5040442. On about 10% of our Windows clients the update would start and go until 96% and stay there for 10-60 minutes, and then after a restart Windows would tell us that something did go wrong and it would reverse the update. This would require multiple restarts and anything in the order of 2-10h. The usual information sources did not reveal anything unusual with this update round, so it had to be some uncommon conditions here. When Windows was back online, it would sometimes (!) show an error code 0x800f0922, oftenly nothing, and on next restart it would try to install it again (and our employees losing again 4-10h with a working computer). First remedy, as described in the error code was to increase the size of the recovery partition to at least 250MB, but that helped only on one computer. No other things related to the code did apply to us or help. DISM and SFC sometimes would find something, but did not help in fixing the issues with the update. Over time some of the computers randomly succeeded in installing the update. Last straw I had was to disable and uninstall Forticlient. And with that so far all of the clients went through the update without a hitch. Now I am anxious that it will return with the next update when I reinstall Forticlient. In retrospective, two computers had some troubles with some previous updates, but we re-installed Windows on them. Both were also affected this time. What should be do and how can we prevent that from happening again? Is there anything to further debug and diagnose this issue? For your reference we use Forticlient 7.2.4.0972 with EMS, and a Fortigate 200F as main firewalls. We have the web filter, AV and real-time protection enabled, as well as Anti-malware, Anti-Exploit and Cloud-base malware protection. Thank you in advance for your help. Regards,Markus

topics.title: Policy Route with SSL VPN interface matches all interfaces' traffic after upgrade to FortiOS version 7.6
topics.summary: DescriptionIf an SSL VPN (Agentless VPN) interface is configured in FortiOS policy routes, the route will match unintended traffic after an upgrade, potentially causing traffic misdirection or drops.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.3 and above.SolutionSSL-VPN tunnel mode is removed in FortiOS version 7.6.3 and above; see SSL VPN tunnel mode replaced with IPsec VPN.In these firmware versions, referencing an SSL VPN or Agentless VPN interface in policy routes is a misconfiguration and will lead to unexpected traffic matches after upgrade.This can cause misrouted or dropped traffic if the route matches unintended traffic. In this case, the route will show an unexpectedly high Hit Count in Network -> Policy Routes after upgrade, while other policy routes may show an unexpectedly low or zero Hit Count. After upgrading from lower FortiOS versions such as FortiOS version 7.4.13 to FortiOS version 7.6.3 or above, SSL VPN interfaces such as ssl.root will be treated as 'any' interface in policy route configuration. This occurs even if the Agentless VPN feature is disabled.Note: If the FortiGate is operating in single VDOM mode, ssl.root is the only Agentless VPN interface. In multi-VDOM operation, an interface is automatically generated for each VDOM.The command diagnose firewall proute list shows Policy and SD-WAN routes:FortiGate-121G # show router policy config router policy edit 1 set input-device "ssl.root" set gateway 10.100.100.1 set output-device "port1" next edit 2 set input-device "Guest WiFi" set output-device "Guest DIA" next end FortiGate-121G # diagnose firewall proute list list route policy info(vf=root): id=1(0x01) dscp_tag=0xfc 0xfc flags=0x0 tos=0x00 tos_mask=0x00 protocol=0 port=src(0->0):dst(0->0) iif=0(any) path(1): oif=5(port1) gwy=10.100.100.1 source wildcard(1): 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 destination wildcard(1): 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 hit_count=264 rule_last_used=2026-10-23 11:15:42 id=2(0x02) dscp_tag=0xfc 0xfc flags=0x0 tos=0x00 tos_mask=0x00 protocol=0 port=src(0->0):dst(0->0) iif=41(Guest WiFi) path(1): oif=40(Guest DIA) source wildcard(1): 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 destination wildcard(1): 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 hit_count=0 rule_last_used=2026-10-23 11:00:16 In the output below, iif=0(any) indicates the route can match inbound traffic over any interface, not just Agentless VPN.id=1(0x01) dscp_tag=0xfc 0xfc flags=0x0 tos=0x00 tos_mask=0x00 protocol=0 port=src(0->0):dst(0->0) iif=0(any) path(1): oif=5(port1) gwy=10.100.100.1 source wildcard(1): 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 destination wildcard(1): 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 hit_count=264 rule_last_used=2026-10-23 11:15:42 Resolution.Go to Network -> Policy Routes and audit the existing Policy Routes. Remove, disable, or reconfigure all policy routes that show 'Agentless VPN' in the Incoming or Outgoing Interface columns. Ideally, do this as part of an IPSec VPN migration before upgrading to FortiOS version 7.6.3 or above. Warning: Use caution when applying routing changes. It is recommended to have an alternate access method to the firewall when editing routes that could affect your administrative access. Do not edit routes that are not well understood.Note: If Network -> Policy Routes is not visible in the GUI, enable 'Advanced Routing' in System -> Feature Visibility and select 'Apply' to expose the page. In CLI, the policy routes can be reviewed using the show router policy command.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Resolution for FortiClient Windows vulnerability CVE-2026-84386
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the impact of CVE-2026-84386 on FortiClient for Windows and provides the necessary versions for remediation.ScopeFortiClient/EMS.SolutionCVE-2026-84386 affects the fortimon3 kernel driver installed with the Antivirus feature of FortiClient for Windows. A locally authenticated administrator can use an anti-exploit communication port exposed by the driver to terminate arbitrary processes. This vulnerability is rated Medium (CVSSv3 4.7), is not remotely exploitable, and requires administrator privileges on the endpoint.Affected versions:FortiClient for Windows v7.4.0 up to v7.4.7.FortiClient for Windows v7.2.0 up to v7.2.1.Fixed versions:FortiClient for Windows v7.4.8.FortiClient for Windows v8.0.0.FortiClient standalone:FortiClient standalone is an unmanaged VPN client that does not include the Antivirus feature. Because the fortimon3 driver belongs to the Antivirus feature, FortiClient Standalone is not exposed to this issue.Verification steps:To verify if an endpoint is vulnerable, perform the following steps:Open a command prompt as administrator.Run the following command: fltmc filters.Check the output for a filter named fortimon3.Verify if the file C:\Windows\System32\drivers\fortimon3.sys exists on the system.If the fortimon3 filter is not listed and the fortimon3.sys file is not present, the vulnerable component is not installed, and no remediation is required.Arbitrary process termination from exposed minifilter communication port

topics.title: Technical Tip: RMA procedure for FortiGates with a single HA license (Single FortiGuard License)
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to perform an RMA for FortiGates that have a single HA license (Single FortiGuard license).ScopeFortiGate.SolutionWhen dealing with failures involving a FortiGate with a single license shared among Cluster/HA members, the license transfer procedure during an RMA differs significantly from the procedure used for a FortiGate with a conventional license. As multiple FortiGate units are covered by the same license, the new FortiGate provided through the RMA cannot be added to the existing single license when the standard RMA process is followed.In this case, when opening a ticket with Fortinet Support, indicate that the firewall has a license shared across the Cluster to prevent automatic license transfer.For instructions on creating a support ticket, refer to Customer Service Tip: How to create a ticket for Fortinet TAC.After opening the ticket and confirming the firewall failure, when transferring the license, follow the steps below:Access Fortinet Support:After logging in, go to Services and select Asset Management.Under Product, select Product List and search for the HA serial number instead of the serial number of the faulty firewall.Select the device and go to RMA Transfer.Select the faulty firewall, either Device 1 or Device 2. Then enter the serial number of the replacement firewall and click Replace. Verify all information and complete the transfer.The license transfer has been completed successfully, allowing the new FortiGate to be added to the cluster and share the same license. For questions regarding this process, contact the FortiCare Support: Customer Service.Related articles:Technical Tip: The HA Cluster license requirementsTechnical Tip: Additional Info regarding Single FortiGuard license for FortiGate A-P HA cluster featureTechnical Tip: FortiGate Models and FortiOS support for HA LicensesTechnical Tip: How to restore a FortiGate HA cluster after RMA

topics.title: Using the FortiGate to protect against PHP vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article discusses the recent critical-severity vulnerabilities for PHP (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, published 2026-10-21) and how the FortiGate can protect affected services until they can be patched.ScopeFortiGate, IPS, OT Virtual Patch;SolutionImportant: Refer to the PSIRT Advisory FG-IR-26-186 regarding the above two CVEs and how they relate to Fortinet products. At the time of this writing, FortiOS itself is not impacted by these PHP-specific CVEs. Instead, this article discusses how the FortiGate can be used to protect other services that do use PHP. At this time, Fortinet has released both IPS signatures and Operational Technology (OT) Virtual Patching signatures for both of the above CVEs. For more information on these signatures, refer to the following entries on the FortiGuard Labs encyclopedia:CVE-2026-109618PHP.longjmp.Remote.Code.Execution (OT Virtual Patch)PHP.longjmp.Remote.Code.Execution (IPS)CVE-2026-109619PHP.stale.global.state.Remote.Code.Execution (OT Virtual Patch)PHP.stale.global.state.Remote.Code.Execution (IPS) Note: Check the above FortiGuard entries for information on the specific database version that introduces support for the associated signatures, then check the FortiGate to ensure that it has updated to a matching or later database version (no firmware updates required). At the time of this writing, support was added as of the following versions:OT Patch Definitions: 37.316(IPS) Attack Definitions and Attack Extended Definitions: 37.317 Once the databases are updated on the FortiGate, the signatures can be checked under Security Profiles -> IPS Signatures: Finally, ensure that the new signatures are loaded into an IPS sensor or Virtual Patching Profile and then assigned to an appropriate Firewall Policy to begin inspecting traffic being sent to your potentially-vulnerable web servers. For more info on configuring IPS sensors and Virtual Patching profiles, refer to the following documentation:Configuring an IPS sensorOT virtual patching basic examples Important:The default action of the IPS-based signatures in definition 37.317 is set to Pass.The default action of the IPS-based signatures in definition 37.319 is set to Drop. (OT Virtual Patch signatures do not include default actions and follow the Action set within the Virtual Patching profile). When adding the signatures to an IPS sensor via rule entries, administrators must change the Action from Default to Block (suggested), Reset, or Quarantine in order to deny the matching traffic: Additionally, consider that SSL Deep Inspection may be required to completely inspect traffic, particularly when forwarding encrypted HTTPS traffic. See also:Protecting an SSL server (FortiGate as an SSL terminator/reverse-proxy)Deep inspection Additional notes:OT Virtual Patching requires a separate license on each FortiGate in order to access the associated signatures (see also: Operational Technology (OT) Datasheet).To validate the version of signature database being used, run the command diagnose autoupdate versions and grep for the related databases:diagnose autoupdate versions | grep OT -A 7 diagnose autoupdate versions | grep Attack -A 7Alternatively, navigate to System -> FortiGuard in the GUI and check under the Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) and Operation Technology (OT) Security Service sections respectively.To manually force an update of the signature databases, run the command execute update-ips in the CLI or navigate to System -> FortiGuard and select Update licenses & definitions now on the right-hand menu.Important: the FortiGate must have an IPS sensor applied in the configuration (e.g. on at least one Firewall Policy) otherwise it will not conduct an update of the IPS database. topics.title: Technical Tip: Update the FortiManager serial number on multiple devices via Script
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to automatically update the FortiManager serial number on multiple FortiGate devices before a license change that causes an FGFM tunnel disconnection and not being able to manage these devices from the FortiManager.ScopeFortiManager, FortiGate.SolutionThere are specific cases when the FortiManager serial number may change due to one of the following situations:VM License expired and a new license was uploaded.VM License is updated via FortiFlex.FortiManager model upgrade or RMA. FortiGate devices associated with the original serial number would be disconnected from the FortiManager and display the status of the FGFM tunnel as down. To resolve this without manually configuring each device, create and run a CLI script to update the central management settings for multiple devices or groups before changing the serial number.Note: In this particular article, the explained case is when the initial FGFM tunnel was initiated only by the FortiGate device. This method will not work if the FortiGate was added from the FortiManager side.There are 2 scenarios when the FortiGate device doesn't have VDOMs and the case when FortiGate has multiple VDOMs. For each case, there will be a slight difference in script content.Case 1 - FortiGate doesn't have VDOMs.Create a CLI script with the following commands:config system central-management set serial-number endReplace with the new FortiManager serial number.Install the script on the group of FortiGate devices without VDOMs.Run the script on the FortiGate devices using the option to run the script on: 'Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)' rather than on the 'Device Database' to ensure the FGFM connection to FortiManager is not lost.Result:-------Executing time: Tue Sep 15 11:39:37 2026----------- Starting log (Run on device) boson-50 (global) config system central-management boson-50 (central-management) set serial-number "FMGVMSTMXXXXXXXX" boson-50 (central-management) end ----------------End of Log------------------------- Case 2 - FortiGate has multiple VDOMs.Create a CLI script with the following commands:config global config system central-management set serial-number endReplace with the new FortiManager serial number.Install the script on the group of FortiGate devices with multiple VDOMs.Run the script on the FortiGate devices. Select the option to run the script on: 'Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)'.Result:-------Executing time: Tue Sep 15 11:39:37 2026----------- Starting log (Run on device) boson-50 config global boson-50 (global) config system central-management boson-50 (central-management) set serial-number "FMGVMSTMXXXXXXXX" boson-50 (central-management) end ----------------End of Log------------------------- Note: There are limitations related to specific CLI commands used in scripts to avoid invalid or sensitive configurations being made on the Device Database. topics.title: FortiGate NTP does not synchronize while devices behind it synchronize normally (UDP/123 filtered upstream)
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to identify an upstream device filtering UDP/123 when FortiGate fails to synchronize its clock while hosts behind the same FortiGate synchronize normally.ScopeFortiOS, FortiGate, system NTP, FortiGuard NTP, packet sniffer, debug flow.SolutionSymptomsFortiGate never synchronizes. Every configured server shows no data.The last synchronization is either never or a timestamp that stops advancing:diagnose sys ntp status execute time # synchronized: no, ntpsync: enabled, server-mode: enabled ipv4 server(ntp1.fortiguard.com) 208.91.112.61 -- unreachable(0x0) S:6 T:193 no data ipv4 server(ntp2.fortiguard.com) 208.91.112.60 -- unreachable(0x0) S:7 T:209 no data ipv4 server(ntp2.fortiguard.com) 208.91.112.62 -- unreachable(0x0) S:6 T:193 no data ipv4 server(ntp1.fortiguard.com) 208.91.112.63 -- unreachable(0x0) S:6 T:193 no data current time is: 12:28:00 last ntp sync:Fri Oct 23 12:17:30 2026At the same time, hosts behind the FortiGate synchronize normally through the same WAN connection. DNS resolution works, the firewall policies allow NTP, and nothing in the FortiGate configuration explains the failure. This combination usually leads the investigation towards FortiGuard, the source-ip setting or FortiOS itself. None of them is the cause.Why only FortiGate is affectedThe NTP client of FortiGate sends its requests from UDP source port 123 to destination port 123 (visible in the capture in step 3), so the replies come back to destination port 123 on the WAN address.Hosts behind FortiGate leave through a firewall policy with NAT enabled. Source NAT replaces their source port with a high port, even when the host itself uses source port 123, and the replies return to that high port.An upstream device — ISP router, CPE or modem — that drops UDP traffic with port 123 on both ends, or inbound traffic to destination port 123, therefore breaks only the NTP traffic generated by FortiGate itself. Filtering NTP on port 123 is a common hardening measure against NTP reflection and amplification, which is why this is seen on otherwise healthy Internet connections.Capture packets on the WAN interfaceStart packet capture and let it run for at least two synchronization attempts:diagnose sniffer packet 'udp port 123' 6 0 lThe signature of this issue is a sequence of outgoing requests from the WAN address with source port 123 and no reply at all:2026-10-23 12:19:24.822796 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.62.123: udp 48 0x0000 xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx 0800 4500 ..............E. 0x0010 004c 0859 0000 4011 218f 0a94 058c d05b .L.Y..@.!....... 0x0020 703e 007b 007b 0038 e188 e300 04fa 0001 p>.{.{.8........ ... 2026-10-23 12:19:24.912967 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.63.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:19:24.912993 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.61.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:19:40.950381 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.60.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:21:10.834202 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.62.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:21:10.916565 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.63.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:21:10.926215 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.61.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:21:26.954348 port3 -- 10.148.5.140.123 -> 208.91.112.60.123: udp 48The sniffer sees packets as they arrive at the interface, before any firewall policy or local-in policy is evaluated. No incoming line from the NTP server means the reply never reached FortiGate. This is also why adding a local-in policy that allows NTP on the WAN interface has no effect.Make sure the captured requests are generated by FortiGateTwo details in the hex output separate FortiGate's own NTP traffic from NTP traffic forwarded on behalf of hosts behind it:On the 0x0010 line, the group 4011 holds the TTL (0x40 = 64) and the protocol (0x11 = UDP). A packet generated by FortiGate leaves with TTL 64. A forwarded packet from a host that sends with TTL 64 leaves with TTL 63 (3f11), because FortiGate decrements it.On the 0x0020 line, 007b 007b is source port 123 and destination port 123. Forwarded traffic leaves with the high port assigned by source NAT.Filter the capture by port, not by the WAN address. A filter on host only catches the post-NAT leg of forwarded traffic, which then looks like traffic generated by FortiGate and leads to the wrong conclusion.Compare with a host behind FortiGateCapture on all interfaces while a host behind FortiGate synchronizes (for example, w32tm /resync on Windows):diagnose sniffer packet any 'udp port 123' 4 0 l 2026-10-23 12:22:11.033121 port4 in 10.134.0.2.123 -> 104.40.149.189.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:22:11.033136 port3 out 10.148.5.140.5240 -> 104.40.149.189.123: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:22:11.070275 port3 in 104.40.149.189.123 -> 10.148.5.140.5240: udp 48 2026-10-23 12:22:11.070294 port4 out 104.40.149.189.123 -> 10.134.0.2.123: udp 48The host sends from source port 123, FortiGate translates it to port 5240, and the reply arrives on the same WAN interface. Same WAN address, same dir

topics.title: FortiGate HA synchronization issue due to system.dns-database checksum mismatch caused by FortiSwitch instability
topics.summary: DescriptionInstability in FortiSwitch connectivity can cause checksum mismatches in the system.dns-database table, leading to FortiGate High Availability (HA) synchronization failures and network outages.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptomsYou may observe the following symptoms:FortiGate HA cluster status repeatedly alternates between synchronized and out-of-sync states.Managed FortiSwitches repeatedly disconnect and reconnect (flapping).Loss of internet connectivity occurs on the primary FortiGate unit, especially if uplinks route through the affected FortiSwitches.HA configuration checksum differences are identified in the system.dns-database table.Root causeInstability in FortiSwitch connectivity can trigger checksum mismatches within the system.dns-database table on FortiGate units. This mismatch prevents the HA cluster from maintaining a synchronized state, which can lead to unexpected failovers and network disruptions.ResolutionStep 1: Verify HA synchronization status.Run the following command on both cluster members to check the HA health and synchronization status:get system ha statusStep 2: Identify the out-of-sync configuration.Compare the checksums between the FortiGate units to isolate the unsynchronized section:diagnose system ha checksum showIf the system.dns-database section shows a mismatch related to a FortiSwitch ID reference, the issue is related to FortiSwitch link instability.Step 3: Resolve FortiSwitch instability.Temporary workaround: Restart the affected FortiSwitches to restore FortiLink stability. After restarting, FortiGate HA synchronization should restore automatically.Permanent solution: The root cause of FortiSwitch link flapping and going offline can often be traced to an NTP daemon defect that consumes high CPU on the switches. To resolve this issue permanently without needing recurring reboots, refer to Managed FortiSwitches go to offline state on the FortiGate due to NTP Daemon consuming high levels of CPU on FortiSwitch and upgrade the FortiSwitch firmware to the recommended fixed releases (such as FortiSwitch 7.4.10, FortiSwitch 7.6.7, FortiSwitch 8.0.1, or higher).Step 4: Verify the resolution.After stabilizing the switches, verify that the HA cluster status returns to synchronized:FortiGate# get system ha statusRelated article:Managed FortiSwitches go to offline state on the FortiGate due to NTP Daemon consuming high levels of CPU on FortiSwitch

topics.title: FortiManager Policy Package install fails with verification error due to "antiphish: max-body-len" parameter
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where FortiManager Policy Package installation fails with a verification error due to the "antiphish: max-body-len" parameter under webfilter profiles.ScopeFortiManager and FortiProxy 7.4.9 and higher, FortiProxy 7.6.1 and higherSolutionWhen installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following:(vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification report install failedThe same message may be reported for multiple webfilter profiles.The root cause is a difference in the default value of the max-body-len parameter between FortiProxy and FortiManager.Starting with FortiProxy 7.4.9 and 7.6.1, the default value of max-body-len was changed from 65535 to 1024. However, FortiManager continues to use 65535 as the default value for this parameter.This difference in default values can result in installation verification failure in FortiManager.To work around the issue, configure FortiManager to use the optimal installation verification mode:config system dm set verify-install optimal end

topics.title: IPv6 local-out traffic failure caused by duplicate default route on PPPoE parent interface with SLAAC
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen a FortiGate interface is configured in dual-stack mode with PPPoE and IPv6 SLAAC autoconfiguration, unencapsulated ICMPv6 Router Advertisements (RAs) from the upstream link can be received directly on the parent underlay interface. When this occurs, FortiOS processes the RA on both the parent underlay interface and the virtual PPPoE interface (pppX), generating a global IPv6 address and installing a default IPv6 kernel route (::/0) for each interface.Because the parent physical underlay cannot route traffic outside the active PPPoE tunnel, self-originating IPv6 traffic generated by the FortiGate (including ping6, DNS, NTP, FortiGuard updates, and TLS active probes for SSL inspection) fails if the system routes packets through the parent interface. Forwarded traffic from internal dual-stack LAN hosts continues to function when policy routing or SD-WAN rules direct outbound sessions through the PPPoE tunnel.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionWhen you configure an interface with set mode pppoe and enable IPv6 autoconfiguration, FortiOS creates a dynamic point-to-point tunnel interface (ppp1 or ppp2) over the parent physical or VLAN interface. In affected releases, the parent underlay interface retains active kernel parameters (accept_ra and autoconf).If an upstream device broadcasts ICMPv6 Router Advertisements as raw Ethernet frames rather than encapsulating them within the PPPoE session, the parent interface accepts the advertisement. This results in the following conditions:The parent interface generates a SLAAC global IPv6 address and installs a default route (::/0) pointing to the upstream link-local gateway.The virtual PPPoE interface concurrently obtains its global IPv6 address and installs a second default route (::/0).FortiOS local-out routing attempts to use the duplicate default routes. Packets exiting the parent interface are sent as unencapsulated Ethernet frames and dropped by the upstream provider.Diagnostic commandsVerify whether the parent interface has accepted an prio=1024 gwy:fe80::9:fff:fe00:402 dev=13(WAN_FTTH) pmtu=0 vf=0 vrf=0 tbl=65534 type=01(unicast) protocol=9(ra) flag=00450000 prio=1024 gwy:fe80::1 dev=17(ppp1) pmtu=0Step 3: Review the complete IPv6 topics.title: SSL connection blocked due to unable to retrieve server certificate in HA Active-Active mode with load-balance enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionHTTPS sessions are reset with an SSL error when processed by the secondary unit in a FortiGate cluster configured for high availability (HA) in active-active mode with flow-based inspection.ScopeFortiOS 7.4+, 7.6+ and 8.0+.SolutionSymptoms:With FortiGate in HA Active-Active mode and load-balance-all enabled, some HTTPS sessions are blocked. Traffic logs show action server-rst and "utmaction=block". The SSL event log shows: "SSL connection is blocked due to unable to retrieve server's certificate".config system ha set mode a-a set sync-packet-balance enable set load-balance-all enable endThis affects only sessions processed by the secondary unit; the primary unit handled sessions normally.In Active-Active mode and with load-balance mode enabled, the secondary unit may process flow-based certificate-inspection sessions. To validate the server certificate, the FortiGate generates a TLS active probe (a local-out connection). Still, the HA mechanism drops this self-originated traffic from the secondary unit with the debug message "local-out traffic, blocked by HA", so the certificate is never retrieved, and the session is blocked.id=65308 trace_id=53 func=print_pkt_detail line=6019 msg="vd-root:0 received a packet(proto=6, 10.5.133.124:19824->13.227.146.62:443) tun_id=0.0.0.0 from local. flag , seq 755531939, ack 0, win 29200" id=65308 trace_id=53 func=init_ip_session_common line=6220 msg="allocate a new session-00007843" id=65308 trace_id=53 func=fw_local_out_handler line=1068 msg="local-out traffic, blocked by HA"Resolution:Allow certificate probe failure: "set cert-probe-failure allow" on the certificate-inspection profile. Maintains connectivity but lowers the inspection security level.config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit config https set cert-probe-failure allow end end endDisable HA load balancing: disable load-balance-all or switch to Active-Passive so the primary handles sessions and probes.config system ha set load-balance-all disable endRelated articles:Troubleshooting Tip: 'local-out traffic, blocked by HA' debug flow messageTroubleshooting Tip: How to fix 'SSL connection is blocked due to unable to retrieve servers certificate' received in the SSL Events

topics.title: Kerberos keytab removed from 'config user krb-keytab' after upgrade from FortiOS v7.6.7 to v7.6.8
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading FortiGate from FortiOS v7.6.7 to v7.6.8, the 'set keytab' line is removed from the Kerberos keytab entries configured under 'config user krb-keytab'. The other settings of each entry (principal, LDAP servers, PAC data) are kept, so the entry is still present in the configuration but without its keytab.Kerberos authentication that relies on an affected entry can fail until the keytab is configured again.ScopeFortiGate, FortiOS v7.6.7 upgraded to v7.6.8, with Kerberos keytab entries configured under 'config user krb-keytab'.An upgrade from v7.6.6 to v7.6.8 is not affected.SolutionThe behavior is reproducible after the upgrade; the keytab of each Kerberos keytab entry is removed from the configuration.After the upgrade, the configuration error log shows a parse error on the 'set keytab' line of each affected entry:FortiGate (global) # diagnose debug config-error-log read >>> "set" "keytab" "ENC" "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX ... @ VDOM_TEST.user.krb-keytab.krb-proxy:command parse error (error -61)The 'ENC' and the encrypted value are read as two separate arguments, and the command is rejected.Configuration before the upgrade (v7.6.7):config user krb-keytab edit "krb-test" set pac-data disable set principal "HTTP/proxy.example.com@EXAMPLE.COM" set ldap-server "LDAP-1" set keytab ENC XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX next endConfiguration after the upgrade (v7.6.8):config user krb-keytab edit "krb-test" set pac-data disable set principal "HTTP/proxy.example.com@EXAMPLE.COM" set ldap-server "LDAP-1" next endRoot cause.The format used to save the 'keytab' value changed between the two versions:FortiOS v7.6.7 saves the value without quotation marks:set keytab ENC XXXXXXXXFortiOS v7.6.8 saves the value as a single quoted string:set keytab "ENC XXXXXXXX"During the upgrade, v7.6.8 parses the configuration saved by v7.6.7. Without the quotation marks, 'ENC' and the encrypted value are read as two separate arguments; the command fails with error -61, and the 'set keytab' line is dropped.FortiOS v7.6.6 already saves the value with quotation marks. As a result, an upgrade from v7.6.6 to v7.6.8 keeps the keytab configuration.Workaround.Configure the keytab again after the upgrade, using one of the following methods.Option 1: Configure the keytab in the CLI, enclosing the value in quotation marks. You can use either the base64-encoded keytab or the encrypted value ('ENC' followed by the string) taken from the configuration backup made before the upgrade:config user krb-keytab edit "krb-proxy" set keytab " " next endOr:config user krb-keytab edit "krb-proxy" set keytab "ENC XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" next endIn multi-VDOM mode, run these commands in the VDOM that holds the entry ('config vdom', then 'edit ').Option 2:Push the Kerberos keytab configuration to the upgraded FortiGate from FortiManager. Before installing, make sure the FortiManager device database still contains the keytab: if the configuration was retrieved from the FortiGate after the upgrade, the keytab may be missing there as well.Verification.Confirm that the 'set keytab' line is present again in each entry:show user krb-keytabAfter any upgrade, check the configuration error log for other Kerberos keytab entries that may be affected:diagnose debug config-error-log read

topics.title: Upgrade firmware fails with "New image is too big"
topics.summary: DescriptionTroubleshooting steps for issues related to the error "New image is too big".ScopeFortiManager-VM, FortiAnalyzer-VM.SolutionTypically, this error occurs during a firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image.This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: "New image is too big”.This is Bug ID 1329518 in the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer Known Issues.Most common causes:Insufficient flash disk space – The flash partition does not have enough free space to store the new firmware image during the upgrade process.Small virtual disk allocation – The VM was originally provisioned with a flash disk that is too small for the target firmware version. Diagnostic steps:Take the firmware update from version 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 for FortiAnalyzer VM as an example.Check flash disk usage:Run the following command on the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer CLI to view the flash disk size and current usage: diagnose system flash list Example output showing the flash disk status:ImageName Version TotalSize(KB) Used(KB) Use% BootImage RunningImage primary FLVM64-8.0-FW-build0105-260420 1006252 592344 59% Yes Yes If the Use% is high or the total size is too small for the target firmware, this confirms the issue. Resolution:Expand the flash disk (FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM). Take a config backup of the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer. Shut down the VM using the following CLI command: execute shutdown Delete all snapshots and wait for the operations to be completed. Expand Disk 1 (or 0) by 4 GB or more in the hypervisor.Note: Do not expand the virtual disk too much, as the additional space will not be available for data. Boot up the VM and verify the flash disk was automatically extended: diagnose system flash list If the VM witnesses File System error occurs, run: diagnose system fsck harddisk Perform the firmware upgrade by manually uploading the firmware image and verify the error no longer appears.

The fix is one global setting: Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points, under System -> Settings -> Network Device.ScopeFortiNAC-F 7.6.x (validated on 7.6.7).FortiGate acting as wireless controller for FortiAPs, modeled in FortiNAC Network -> Inventory.FortiAPs connected to a third-party access switch (example: Aruba CX 6200) that uses FortiNAC as RADIUS server for MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB).SolutionSymptoms:The FortiAP's switch port stays in the static access VLAN instead of moving to the VLAN set in the Network Access Policy.The FortiAP appears under the FortiGate in Network -> Inventory as a Wireless Access Point.Searching the AP MAC in Users & Hosts -> Hosts returns nothing.Device Profiling Rules (for example Vendor OUI, type Wireless Access Point) never process the AP.Network Access Policies whose User/Host Profile matches the AP MAC never match.Deleting the AP from Inventory makes the policy work temporarily; the AP returns under the FortiGate at the next poll or reconnect.The RADIUS log shows an Access-Accept with no VLAN attributes (example values):[Access-Request] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ User-Name = aabbccddeeff, Service-Type = Call-Check, Calling-Station-Id = AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF, NAS-Identifier = ACCESS-SW-01, NAS-Port-Type = Ethernet, NAS-Port-Id = 1/1/2 ] [Access-Accept] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ REST-HTTP-Status-Code = 200, Cleartext-Password = "aabbccddeeff", Class = 0x..., Hint = "...", Tmp-String-1 = "request" ]The Access-Accept carries no Tunnel-Type, Tunnel-Medium-Type or Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, so the switch keeps the port in its default VLAN.Cause:This is expected behavior. FortiNAC models FortiGate-managed FortiAPs as network devices (Inventory elements), not as hosts. When a Wireless Access Point connects to a managed switch port, FortiNAC changes the port type to WAP Uplink.By default, FortiNAC does not evaluate Network Access Policies for Wireless Access Points and does not enforce any policy on a WAP Uplink port. With no host record and no applicable policy, the MAB Access-Accept carries no VLAN.SolutionEnable Network Access Policy evaluation for Wireless Access Points. No other change is required when the Network Access Policy and port configuration are already in place.In the FortiNAC GUI, go to System -> Settings -> Network Device.Select Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points.Select Save Settings.Confirm the switch port where the FortiAP connects is a member of the Role-Based Access port group. This is required for the setting to take effect.Optional: Set Wireless Access Point Enforcement Group to a port group. FortiNAC adds a port to it when a Wireless Access Point connects; it does not remove the port automatically.Reconnect the FortiAP or bounce its switch port so a new MAB request is sent.Verification:The RADIUS Access-Accept for the AP MAC now includes Tunnel-Type = VLAN, Tunnel-Medium-Type = IEEE-802 and Tunnel-Private-Group-ID = the policy VLAN.Network -> Inventory -> switch -> Ports: The AP port shows the expected VLAN, and Port Changes records the change.Verify the VLAN assigned to the switch port interface.Notes:Deleting FortiAPs from Inventory is not a workaround; FortiNAC re-adds them under the FortiGate.The AP port must not be in the Authorized Access Points group, which prevents VLAN switching on the port.If the port is also in Reset Forced Default, set its Default VLAN equal to the policy VLAN to avoid the VLAN cycling between the two.Confirm RADIUS and VLAN switching are enabled in the switch Model Configuration, with a RADIUS attribute group that includes RFC VLAN attributes.Tunnel-mode SSIDs are preferred. With bridge-mode SSIDs, wireless client MACs also appear on the AP port, which can affect port classification and MAB on the switch.Alternative: Network Device Roles (role assigned to the FortiAP + mapping by port group and VLAN), with the port in Role-Based Access.Related articles:Administration Guide (FortiNAC-F 7.6): Network device settingsAdministration Guide (FortiNAC-F 7.6): Network device rolesWAP behavior when connected to WAP Uplink ports

topics.title: Technical Tip: How to configure Network ID for distinguishing IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels using FortiClient XML file
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article explains how to edit the FortiClient XML file to distinguish multiple IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels using Network ID instead of Peer ID.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient.SolutionWhen multiple dial-up IPsec IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels are configured on FortiGate, a unique Network ID must be defined on each Phase 1 configuration. This allows FortiGate to correctly match incoming IKEv2 initiations with the appropriate tunnel.If the Network ID is not defined, FortiGate cannot reliably determine which Phase 1 configuration to use when multiple IKEv2 dial‑up tunnels reside on the same interface. This behavior differs from IKEv1, where Peer IDs were used to distinguish between tunnels. Use the following CLI syntax to define the Network ID for each Phase 1 configuration: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit " " set ike-version 2 set network-overlay enable set network-id next end The Network ID must be defined on both the FortiGate Phase1 and the FortiClient configuration to ensure correct tunnel matching.Note: The Network ID setting cannot be configured on unmanaged or standalone Forticlient. For managed Forticlient, configuration of Network ID is supported through Forticlient EMS starting with versions 7.2.6 and later or 7.4.1 and later.The FortiClient XML configuration file can be manually edited or provisioned via EMS with the Network ID attribute. Locate the section of the XML, and insert the tag as shown below.Note: Occasionally, this value is not included in the configuration. topics.title: Preserving client IP addresses across AP group VLANs with Layer 3 intra controller roaming
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to enable a new Layer 3 intra-controller roaming feature on a bridge-mode SSID, so wireless clients can move between FortiAP groups that are mapped to different VLANs, while retaining their original IP address.ScopeFortiGate 60F with FortiOS 7.4.11 and two FortiAP-441K access points with FortiAP firmware 7.6.3, managed by the same FortiGate.The source lab used feature-specific STS builds. The version labels above identify the tested release families and do not establish support in every build. Confirm that the target build exposes 'l3-intra-roaming' before applying this configuration.Solution1. Prepare the environmentUse two authorized FortiAPs managed by the same FortiGate and broadcasting the same bridge-mode SSID. Configure the SSID authentication before applying the following changes. The selected test used WPA2 Personal.Create two managed AP groups and assign one access point to each:FortiAPAP groupClient VLANManagement IPFAP1-loungeNorth10010.10.201.2FAP2-officeSouth20010.10.202.2Provide the required VLANs, DHCP scopes, gateways, and routing. Ensure the FortiAPs can communicate directly, without NAT in the path, when using direct roaming mode.Advertise the SSID on both access points. The tested 5 GHz channels were 140 and 132. Adjust transmit power to provide overlapping coverage and allow the client to select another access point when moving. Check the RF environment before starting the test.2. Map the AP groups to VLANs and enable intra-controller roamingOn the FortiGate, edit the existing SSID object. Replace with its configured name. The groups North and South must already exist and contain the corresponding access points.config wireless-controller vap edit " " set local-bridging enable set vlan-pooling wtp-group config vlan-pool edit 100 set wtp-group "North" next edit 200 set wtp-group "South" next end set l3-roaming enable set l3-intra-roaming enable set l3-roaming-mode direct next endThe key setting is 'set l3-intra-roaming enable' in the SSID configuration. The VLAN pool associates each participating AP group with its local client VLAN. Configure both groups; enabling the roaming setting alone does not replace this mapping.These changes modify an existing SSID, not a complete SSID creation script. Preserve the existing authentication and radio assignments. Review existing VLAN pool entries before applying the example.3. Validate IP preservationConnect a client to the SSID and record its IP address, associated FortiAP, and VLAN. Start a continuous connectivity test to a reachable destination. Move the client between the coverage areas, then return to the original access point.In the FortiGate wireless client monitor, compare the IP, FortiAP, FortiAP IP, and VLAN fields. The access point and local VLAN context should change while the client IP remains unchanged during the roaming test.Figure 1: iPhone test across FAP1-lounge (VLAN 100) and FAP2-office (VLAN 200). Both records show the client IP 10.10.200.3. Customer SSID labels are redacted.Figure 2: The iPhone is shown back on FAP2-office in VLAN 200 with the same IP, 10.10.200.3.Figure 3: Android test showing the same client IP, 10.10.100.2, across the two FortiAPs and VLAN contexts.Figure 4: Windows test showing client IP 10.10.200.4 across the same VLAN 100 and VLAN 200 roaming path. Customer SSID and personal device labels are redacted.The tested monitor sometimes retained duplicate client records after roaming. The paired rows show the observed IP and VLAN contexts; they do not prove simultaneous associations. Correlate the monitor with reassociation events and the client-side connectivity test.ResultThe selected local-lab test successfully validated roaming between North/VLAN 100 and South/VLAN 200 with iPhone, Android, and Windows clients retaining their original IP addresses. The report also records successful return to the original access point.IP preservation applies to the tested roaming sequence. It does not imply that a client keeps its address indefinitely after disconnecting or rehoming. The results do not establish zero packet loss or a universal roaming-time guarantee.

topics.title: Capturing Zebra ZS300 BLE data with FortiAP for temperature monitoring
topics.summary: DescriptionConfigure BLE scanning on a FortiAP to collect advertisements from Zebra ZS300 temperature sensors for processing and visualization by an external application.ScopeThe main proof of concept used a FortiGate 60F running FortiOS 7.4.12 and a FortiAP-233G running firmware 7.4.5. A separate local validation used a FortiAP-234F.The workflow illustrates BLE scanning on both models. Configuration availability depends on the FortiAP model and firmware.Solution1. Configure BLE scanningOn the FortiGate, create a BLE profile using the scan parameters validated during the proof of concept:config wireless-controller ble-profile edit "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" set ble-scanning enable set scan-type active set scan-threshold "-90" set scan-period 4000 set scan-time 1000 set scan-interval 50 set scan-window 50 next endAssign the BLE profile to the FortiAP profile. Replace with the existing profile name.config wireless-controller wtp-profile edit " " set ble-profile "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" next endIf the FortiAP profile is shared, this change affects the other access points using it.2. Verify the BLE configurationFrom the FortiAP CLI, run:cw_diag -c ble-configThe following excerpt shows the scan configuration observed during the main proof of concept:WTP Bluetooth Low Energy Configuration: ble scan report interval : 30 ble scanning : enabled (mode=active,thresh=-90,period=4000,time=1000,intv=50,wind=50)BLE scanning must be enabled. The iBeacon and Eddystone advertising settings also displayed by this command describe advertisements transmitted by the FortiAP and are not required to interpret the Zebra sensor data.3. Verify sensor receptionPlace the active sensor within BLE coverage and run:cw_diag -c ble-scanThe following output is transcribed from the local validation screenshot:BLE_DEV (001/001), mac ce:c3:25:fc:4e:a0 gen : 1 rssi : -88 addr type : random name : GEOMOV14587_LE manufacture : first seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 last seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 channel : 38 raw data : 22 0201020f0947454f 4d4f563134353837 5f4c45020a00Use the known sensor MAC address and its serial-number mapping in the sensor inventory to identify the intended device. Check the reception timestamps, RSSI, and raw data field.For devices using random BLE addresses, verify the identity mapping instead of assuming that the displayed address remains permanent.Figure 1: BLE configuration and scan output from the FortiAP-234F used for local validation. The main laboratory used a FortiAP-233G. The screenshot illustrates the scan workflow on another model; it does not independently demonstrate Zebra temperature decoding.4. Display temperature dataDuring the proof of concept, an external collector accessed the FortiAP over SSH through an IPsec VPN and retrieved BLE scan output every five seconds. The external application identified the Zebra sensor, processed the captured payload, and displayed temperature information in a dashboard.The FortiAP provided BLE scan data. The external application decoded the payload, stored historical data, and visualized it on a dashboard.Figure 2: Dashboard supplied as evidence of the proof of concept. The displayed period includes 12,044 events, an average RSSI of -78 dBm, an average battery level of 68.5%, and an average temperature of -19.01 °C. The dashboard also displays a mean kinetic temperature of -19.18 °C. These values are aggregated metrics, not individual instantaneous measurements.Note: Restrict SSH access to the authorized collector and protect its credentials. The five-second collection interval is independent of the BLE report interval shown by ble-config and does not guarantee a new temperature measurement on each query. Validate collection performance and the automation method before production deployment.

topics.title: Unable to save configuration with “execute cfg save” when using FortiGateCloud or FortiManager CLI script
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen configuration save mode on the FortiGate (aka cfg-save under config system global) is changed from automatic to either manual or revert, any configuration changes applied via CLI scripts pushed from FortiGate Cloud or FortiManager may not be saved to flash.ScopeFortiOS 7.2.x, 7.4.x, and 7.6.x.SolutionAs a quick primer: cfg-save is a configurable feature that allows FortiGate administrators to enforce manual saving of configuration changes to persistent storage, as opposed to the default behavior where the FortiGate automatically saves each change once it is committed. For more info, refer to the following Article: Technical Tip: Using the save option 'set cfg-save revert' to automatically reboot and revert to a previous configuration of a FortiGate config system global set cfg-save end However, there is currently an issue where cfg-save (when set to manual or revert) can have an unexpected interaction with CLI scripts that are pushed to the FortiGate using FortiManagement Cloud (previously known as FortiGate Cloud) or FortiManager. After a CLI script is run, the configuration changes will appear in the running configuration, but those changes are not currently being written to flash/persistent storage. As a result, those changes do not appear when a configuration backup is taken and will be lost if the FortiGate is rebooted. Note: The cfg-revert-timeout used in revert mode is not triggered in this scenario: config system global set cfg-save revert set cfg-revert-timeout 7200 end Demonstration of issue:As an example, the following CLI script modifies a firewall address group and attempts to save the configuration. config firewall addrgrp edit "OBJ_GRP" append member "OBJ_1" "OBJ_2" set allow-routing enable next end execute cfg save The script is then executed through either FortiManagement Cloud or FortiManager, after which the script execution output can be reviewed. Notably, the commandexecute cfg save may state the message "no config to be saved": FW01 config firewall addrgrp FW01 (addrgrp) edit "OBJ_GRP" FW01 (OBJ_GRP) append member "OBJ_1" "OBJ_2" FW01 (OBJ_GRP) set allow-routing enable FW01 (OBJ_GRP) next FW01 (addrgrp) end FW01 execute cfg save no config to be saved. Gathering diagnostic info:To collect diagnostic output to match this behaviour, run the following commands before running the CLI script to reproduce the issue: diagnose debug reset diagnose debug cli 8 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug enable diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset See also: Technical Tip: Verify applied configuration change in CLI Resolution:This issue has been identified and will be resolved in the following upcoming FortiOS versions. Once available, upgrade the FortiGate to one of the following versions:FortiOS 7.6.9FortiOS 8.0.3 Workaround:Until a fixed FortiOS release is available, use one of the following workarounds:Save the configuration manually: Until fixed firmware is applied, perform the configuration changes directly on the FortiGate (GUI or SSH), rather than via CLI script from a management platform.Use automatic configuration saving: Temporarily change the global cfg-save setting to automatic before executing future CLI scripts. Restore the required configuration save mode after validating the behavior and operational requirements. Related article:Technical Tip: Configuration file save mode for configuration changes

topics.title: RMA Information: Hardware failure and replacement with a spare unit on-site (support procedure)
topics.summary: Description This KB article describes, how to manage an RMA request (a hardware replacement request within the technical support contract) with the Fortinet Customer Service and Support (Fortinet CSS), when another (possibly temporary) spare unit is already available on-site. In case of a hardware failure on a Fortinet product and a need for replacement, when a spare unit is already available on-site (for example: a "cold spare" unit, or a temporarily loaned unit from a Fortinet reseller or distributor), for a smooth RMA exchange of the defective unit by the Fortinet CSS, Fortinet recommends to proceed as follows: 1. With the Fortinet CSS, create an RMA ticket first, using the serial number of the defective unit.2. In the RMA ticket, describe the problem with the defective unit, and make sure to mention to which spare/replacement unit (specify the serial number) the support contract will be transferred to.3. Once the RMA ticket has been created, request the Fortinet Customer Service (Fortinet CS) to transfer the support contract from the defective unit to the spare unit, possibly by creating another ticket (this time, a CS ticket), or making a phone call. topics.title: Using BGP route maps to switch branch application traffic from production to disaster recovery
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to configure inbound BGP route maps on a branch FortiGate to prefer a disaster recovery (DR) site over a production site for a specific application network.ScopeAll FortiGatesSolutionBoth sites advertise the same prefix. Production remains available as a backup path.Prerequisites:Both BGP sessions are established and advertise 172.16.100.0/24 to the branch.Both paths have reachable next hops and equal BGP weight.The application can operate at DR using the same destination addresses. topics.summary: DescriptionHow to disable unwanted FortiToken activation emails for FortiClient Standalone users provisioned in FortiIdentity Cloud that use an external Identity Provider for MFA.ScopeFortiIdentity Cloud (formerly FortiTokenCloud), FortiClient Standalone.SolutionTo prevent FortiToken activation emails from being sent, configure FortiIdentity Cloud to use the remote Identity Provider for all authentication by enabling passthrough mode:Log in to the FortiIdentity Cloud console.Go to Applications -> SSO.Edit the SSO application or create a new SSO application.Set the authentication setting to Passthrough.This configuration ensures that FortiIdentity Cloud does not attempt to manage passwords or MFA tokens locally, which suppresses the automatic sending of FortiToken activation emails.

incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes why, in some scenarios, certificate-based dialup IPsec authentication may fail after upgrading to FortiOS versions 7.6.7 or 7.4.12 when the PKI peer is configured with cn-type FQDN.ScopeFortiGate, certificate-based dialup IPsec VPN.SolutionCertificate-based IPsec VPN utilizes mutual certificate-based authentication to validate the certificate chain presented during the IKE authentication.
incidents.symptom: This article describes why, in some scenarios, certificate-based dialup IPsec authentication may fail after upgrading to FortiOS versions 7.6.7 or 7.4.12 when the PKI peer is configured with cn-type FQDN
incidents.solution: Certificate-based IPsec VPN utilizes mutual certificate-based authentication to validate the certificate chain presented during the IKE authentication. The accepted CA certificate and Common Name information of client certificate should be configured under the 'config user peer' to be referenced by the IPsec configuration.When a PKI peer uses cn-type FQDN on the Diapup IPsec VPN hub FortiGate, it not only checks the certificate name but also compares the hostname’s mapped IP address with the connecting client’s IP address.For example:config user peer edit "BRANCH-PEER" set ca "VPN-CA" set subject "CN=branch01.example.com" set cn "branch01.example.com" set cn-type FQDN next endFor authentication to succeed, the hub must resolve the peer's Common Name (CN) 'branch01.example.com' to the connecting peer’s IP address as seen by the hub. incidents.symptom: If an SSL VPN (Agentless VPN) interface is configured in FortiOS policy routes, the route will match unintended traffic after an upgrade, potentially causing traffic misdirection or drops
incidents.solution: SSL-VPN tunnel mode is removed in FortiOS version 7.6.3 and above; see SSL VPN tunnel mode replaced with IPsec VPN.In these firmware versions, referencing an SSL VPN or Agentless VPN interface in policy routes is a misconfiguration and will lead to unexpected traffic matches after upgrade.This can cause misrouted or dropped traffic if the route matches unintended traffic. In this case, the route will show an unexpectedly high Hit Count in Network -> Policy Routes after upgrade, while other policy routes may show an unexpectedly low or zero Hit Count. After upgrading from lower FortiOS versions such as FortiOS version 7.4.13 to FortiOS version 7.6.3 or above, SSL VPN interfaces such as ssl.root will be treated as 'any' interface in policy route configuration. This occurs even if the Agentless VPN feature is disabled.Note: If the FortiGate is operating in single VDOM mode, ssl.root is the only Agentless VPN interface. In multi-VDOM operation, an interface is automatically generated for each VDOM.The command diagnose firewall proute list shows Policy and SD-WAN routes:FortiGate-121G # show router policy config router policy edit 1 set input-device "ssl.root" set gateway 10.100.100.1 s
