incidents.symptom: When a FortiGate interface is configured in dual-stack mode with PPPoE and IPv6 SLAAC autoconfiguration, unencapsulated ICMPv6 Router Advertisements (RAs) from the upstream link can be received directly on the parent underlay interface. When this occurs, FortiOS processes the RA on both the parent underlay interface and the virtual PPPoE interface (pppX), generating a global IPv6 address and installing a default IPv6 kernel route (::/0) for each interface.Because the parent physical underlay cannot route traffic outside the active PPPoE tunnel, self-originating IPv6 traffic generated by the FortiGate (including ping6, DNS, NTP, FortiGuard updates, and TLS active probes for SSL inspection) fails if the system routes packets through the parent interface. Forwarded traffic from internal dual-stack LAN hosts continues to function when policy routing or SD-WAN rules direct outbound sessions through the PPPoE tunnel
incidents.solution: When you configure an interface with set mode pppoe and enable IPv6 autoconfiguration, FortiOS creates a dynamic point-to-point tunnel interface (ppp1 or ppp2) over the parent physical or VLAN interface. In affected releases, the parent underlay interface retains active kernel parameters (accept_ra and autoconf).If an upstream device broadcasts ICMPv6 Router Advertisements as raw Ethernet frames rather than encapsulating them within the PPPoE session, the parent interface accepts the advertisement. This results in the following conditions:The parent interface generates a SLAAC global IPv6 address and installs a default route (::/0) pointing to the upstream link-local gateway.The virtual PPPoE interface concurrently obtains its global IPv6 address and installs a second default route (::/0).FortiOS local-out routing attempts to use the duplicate default routes. Packets exiting the parent interface are sent as unencapsulated Ethernet frames and dropped by the upstream provider.Diagnostic commandsVerify whether the parent interface has accepted an unencapsulated Router Advertisement:Step 1: Check assigned IPv6 addresses:diagnose ipv6 address listIn an affected state, both the parent in Contournement : ).Decouple PPPoE from the physical or VLAN interface by creating a dedicated system pppoe-interface. This stops the parent interface from processing raw Router Advertisements.Remove PPPoE mode and IPv6 autoconfiguration from the parent interface:config system interface edit "WAN_FTTH" set vdom "root" set mode static set type vlan set interface "port3" set vlanid 10 config ipv6 set ip6-mode static end next endCreate a dedicated PPPoE interface linked to the parent device:config system pppoe-interface edit "PPPOE_WAN" set ipv6 enable set device "WAN_FTTH" set username "user@example.com" set password "SecurePassword123" next endConfigure IPv6 settings on the generated PPPoE interface:config system interface edit "PPPOE_WAN" set vdom "root" set mode pppoe set type tunnel config ipv6 set ip6-allowaccess ping set autoconf enable set dhcp6-prefix-delegation enable config dhcp6-iapd-list edit 1 set prefix-hint ::/56 next end end next endNotes:The parent interface stops processing raw RAs because its IPv6 autoconfiguration is disabled.The PPPOE_WAN tunnel interface handles SLAAC and prefix delegation.Update firewall policies, static routes, and SD-WAN members to u

incidents.summary: DescriptionWhen configuration save mode on the FortiGate (aka cfg-save under config system global) is changed from automatic to either manual or revert, any configuration changes applied via CLI scripts pushed from FortiGate Cloud or FortiManager may not be saved to flash.ScopeFortiOS 7.2.x, 7.4.x, and 7.6.x.SolutionAs a quick primer: cfg-save is a configurable feature that allows FortiGate administrators to enforce manual saving of configuration changes to persistent storage, as opposed to the default behavior where the FortiGate automatically saves…
incidents.symptom: When configuration save mode on the FortiGate (aka cfg-save under config system global) is changed from automatic to either manual or revert, any configuration changes applied via CLI scripts pushed from FortiGate Cloud or FortiManager may not be saved to flash
incidents.solution: As a quick primer: cfg-save is a configurable feature that allows FortiGate administrators to enforce manual saving of configuration changes to persistent storage, as opposed to the default behavior where the FortiGate automatically saves each change once it is committed. For more info, refer to the following Article: Technical Tip: Using the save option 'set cfg-save revert' to automatically reboot and revert to a previous configuration of a FortiGate config system global set cfg-save end However, there is currently an issue where cfg-save (when set to manual or revert) can have an unexpected interaction with CLI scripts that are pushed to the FortiGate using FortiManagement Cloud (previously known as FortiGate Cloud) or FortiManager. After a CLI script is run, the configuration changes will appear in the running configuration, but those changes are not currently being written to flash/persistent storage. As a result, those changes do not appear when a configuration backup is taken and will be lost if the FortiGate is rebooted. Note: The cfg-revert-timeout used in revert mode is not triggered in this scenario: config system global set cfg-save revert set cfg-revert-timeout 7200 en Contournement : Until a fixed FortiOS release is available, use one of the following workarounds:Save the configuration manually: Until fixed firmware is applied, perform the configuration changes directly on the FortiGate (GUI or SSH), rather than via CLI script from a management platform.Use automatic configuration saving: Temporarily change the global cfg-save setting to automatic before executing future CLI scripts. Restore the required configuration save mode after validating the behavior and operational requirements. Related article:Technical Tip: Configuration file save mode for configuration changes

incidents.symptom: On FortiGate ZTNA Access Proxies configured with TCP forwarding and SAML authentication, client authentication attempts can fail with Error 021: Application not found (HTTP 403 Forbidden). This error occurs when the client browser reaches the FortiGate Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) endpoint (/remote/saml/login/), but the Web Access Daemon (WAD) proxy engine fails to route the request to the internal SAML service provider gateway.This behavior occurs because FortiOS dynamically registers the implicit SAML Service Provider virtual host only when the SAML Service Provider endpoints are configured with a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN). When a literal IP address is used in the SAML single-sign-on-url, or when the SAML hostname collides with an existing reverse-proxy virtual host, WAD drops the request with a "No matched gwy" condition. You can resolve this issue by assigning a dedicated public FQDN to the SAML Service Provider configuration
